---
title: TPU Training (Experimental)
description: Running Axolotl on Google Cloud TPUs
---

> **Experimental.** This guide is written ahead of end-to-end TPU testing. Once TPU access is confirmed the experimental caveats will be removed.

## Prerequisites

- A Google Cloud TPU VM (v4-8, v5e-8, or v6e-8 recommended for single-host data-parallel training).
- Python 3.11+ with `torch>=2.13,<2.15` pre-installed (use a TPU Deep Learning VM image).

## Installation

```bash
pip install "axolotl[tpu]" -f https://storage.googleapis.com/libtpu-releases/index.html
```

On a TPU Deep Learning VM the `libtpu` wheel is pre-installed; the find-links flag above provides it for fresh installs.

## Quick start

```bash
PJRT_DEVICE=TPU axolotl train examples/tpu/llama-3-1b-lora.yml
```

`axolotl train` detects `torch_xla` at import time and automatically:

- Passes `--tpu` to `accelerate launch`, which spawns one worker per TPU chip via `xmp.spawn`.
- Sets `PJRT_DEVICE=TPU` if not already in the environment.
- Enables bf16 (all current TPU generations support bfloat16 natively).
- Pads every batch to exactly `sequence_len` so XLA never recompiles on a new shape.
- Drops the final incomplete batch (`dataloader_drop_last: true`).

## Minimal config

```yaml
base_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
adapter: lora

# TPU-safe attention (eager or sdpa; no flash-attn)
attn_implementation: sdpa

# Precision
bf16: true

# Static shapes (required on TPU; auto-set, but explicit is clearer)
pad_to_sequence_len: true
sequence_len: 2048

datasets:
  - path: tatsu-lab/alpaca
    type: alpaca

output_dir: ./outputs/lora-tpu
```

See `examples/tpu/` for complete, ready-to-run configs.

## Supported features

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| SFT (supervised fine-tuning) | ✅ |
| LoRA | ✅ |
| Full fine-tuning | ✅ |
| bf16 | ✅ |
| Data parallel (all chips on one host) | ✅ |
| `gradient_checkpointing: true` | ✅ |
| Resume from checkpoint | ✅ |
| `merge-lora` / `inference` (on CPU) | ✅ |
| `preprocess` | ✅ |

## Not yet supported

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| QLoRA / bitsandbytes | BnB requires CUDA |
| Flash Attention | CUDA kernel; use `attn_implementation: sdpa` |
| DeepSpeed | Not applicable on TPU |
| FSDP / FSDPv2 | Planned follow-up |
| Sample packing | Dynamic shapes cause recompilation |
| RL training (DPO, GRPO, …) | Planned follow-up |
| `torch_compile` | XLA is already a compiler |
| Multi-host TPU pods | Planned follow-up |
| Trainium (AWS) | Separate effort |

Axolotl will raise a clear error at config-validation time if you use an unsupported feature.

## Diagnosing recompilation

The first two training steps always compile. After that, you should see no new compilations. Check with:

```python
import torch_xla.debug.metrics as met
print(met.short_metrics_report())
```

or set `PT_XLA_DEBUG_LEVEL=1` in the environment for per-step logging.

The most common cause of steady-state recompilation is a shape change in the input batch.
`pad_to_sequence_len: true` (auto-set on TPU) prevents the most common case. If you see
recompilation, add `PT_XLA_DEBUG_LEVEL=2` and look for `XLAGraph` lines with different shapes.

## Troubleshooting

**`RuntimeError: No CUDA/mps/npu/xla device found`**: `torch_xla` is not installed, or
`USE_TORCH_XLA=0` is set. Check `pip show torch_xla` and unset `USE_TORCH_XLA`.

**`NotImplementedError: qlora is not supported on TPU`**: Switch to `adapter: lora`.

**Slow first steps**: Normal. XLA compiles the computation graph on the first one or two steps;
subsequent steps are fast.

**`accelerate launch` errors**: Make sure `PJRT_DEVICE=TPU` is set and `torch_xla` is importable.
Run `python -c "import torch_xla; print(torch_xla.__version__)"` to verify.
